<!--
Read, not measured: a table with a cell too long for one line of the source
gets its columns' widths from the dashes under its head, and pandoc writes
them to Word as a fixed layout. The short Num column got too few to hold its
heading once Word took its cell margins out, and Word set it as "Nu" over
"m" (docxcolumnwidths.lua). It is widened to hold the word, and the wide
column gives up the room.

The second table's columns already hold their words, and its widths are
left as pandoc wrote them. Its first row holds a non-breaking space, which
the filter once cut in two, failing the render, where a system's %s takes
its second byte for a space.
-->

| Headshort | A heading long enough that it has to wrap onto a second line here, and then words headend | Num |
|:----------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------|----:|
| Bodyshort | Bodystart a body cell long enough that it has to wrap onto a second line inside its column | 12.5 |
| Rowtwo    | 2                                                                    | 3.0  |

: Narrow caption {#tbl-narrow}

| Item       | A column with a cell long enough to make pandoc give the table widths of its own here | Value     |
|:-----------|:--------------------------------------------------------|----------:|
| Row\ 1     | short                                                  | 1.00      |
